free_tier.stated: 10 GiB free storage per project on GitLab.com Free tier (repo + LFS); snippet files up to 50 MB each (50,000,000-byte default admin limit); projects per account and accounts are free.

egress.terms: unmetered, served from gitlab.com; no egress line item exists on any GitLab.com plan.

tooling: glab CLI (glab snippet create), VS Code extension, REST /api/v4/snippets, plain git clone/push for project repos. rclone has a 'gitlab' backend (yes — rclone supports GitLab as a Git remote type via backend 'git').
chaining: 10 GiB free per project x unlimited projects per free account x unlimited free accounts. Snippets add a parallel 50 MB-per-object path that does not require a project.
limits_note: 10 GiB per project then the project goes read-only (pushes rejected) until storage is purchased — a hard stop, not a warning; 50 MB per snippet; namespace storage updated every 90 minutes; 5 GiB per-file push limit on gitlab.com is not documented publicly, so shard files.
reliability_note: Read-only lockout is automatic and immediate on exceeding 10 GiB, and it blocks pushes rather than deletes data. Snippets are counted in namespace storage, so they are not a separate free pool.

evidence.proved: 'Each project in a Free tier namespace on GitLab.com has 10 GiB of free storage', 'the project is set to a read-only state'
probe: GET -> {"message":"401 Unauthorized"} (authenticated endpoints only; public snippet read via web returned 200)
